slips.title: The farthing in the wick
slips.opening: Mabry fishes a tiny coin out of the dead lamp. It has left a green circle on her last receipt. “My boy thinks I can light it by paying it.”
slips.first: Rub the circle onto the back of the receipt
slips.discovery: Three cuts on the coin match the places where the lamp used to hold a strip of paper.

routes.action: Hang the rubbing on the lamp rail
routes.consequence: Mabry leaves it low enough for her boy to touch. Her first customer asks if she stole a coin.

routes.action: Put the original in Mabry’s apron pocket
routes.consequence: Mabry lets her boy feel the edge. A stranger has to ask her before trying it.

slips.title: The envelope with a little sun
slips.opening: Wystan has been scraping the return label for most of the afternoon. On the back a child has drawn a round lamp with three rays.
slips.first: Hold the envelope to the reed screen
slips.discovery: There is space between the rays for a folded instruction. Wystan used to work the lamp before the river posting.

routes.action: Copy the three rays at the returns desk
routes.consequence: A visiting keeper can find the pocket. Wystan turns his old duty badge face down.

routes.action: Ask Wystan to keep the drawing with the letter
routes.consequence: He puts the paper back in the right hands. Nobody outside the old crew knows the pocket is there.

slips.title: Snow on a dry-year slip
slips.opening: Osric will let you take off one glove. He keeps the other around a name on the catchment slip. The family who wrote it are still waiting to be paid.
slips.first: Ease the tissue off the dash between the dates
slips.discovery: A dry-year proviso continues into a clean-edged gap. The paper has been cut twice, first with blunt kitchen shears.

routes.action: Show the cut beneath the family’s folded name
routes.consequence: People can see what went missing. Osric has promised to stand beside the fold all day.

routes.action: Give the family the tissue with the impression
routes.consequence: Osric gets a thank-you meant for somebody who died years ago. He has to arrange a second viewing.

slips.title: A boat drawn at two waterlines
slips.opening: Astor wants the harbour portrait in tomorrow’s fair. The painter drew Elsbet above a second set of wet boots and never painted in the person wearing them.
slips.first: Set the little tide mirror level with the lower boot
slips.discovery: The painter left room for someone kneeling beside Elsbet. Gold foil on the heel came from a press, not a uniform.

routes.action: Hang the trial portrait with the empty space visible
routes.consequence: Someone will ask who was kneeling. Astor gives up the chance to sell a finished picture.

routes.action: Let the pilot see the working sketch first
routes.consequence: The pilot recognises the turn in the sole. The fair opens with an empty hook.

slips.title: An invoice that sings
slips.opening: A bird in Gale’s observation blind whistles three notes whenever the old cash box shuts. Gale holds it open. “Nobody borrowed a tune from a bird with an invoice in its foot.”
slips.first: Close the lid over the carbon paper
slips.discovery: Three notches on the lid strike three pitches. The carbon caught the last loop of a customer's signature.

routes.action: Play the three-note receipt at the watch post
routes.consequence: Gale’s assistant can challenge the result in daylight. Every visitor starts whistling the tune.

routes.action: Carry the silent carbon in the cash box
routes.consequence: The customer’s loop stays intact. Only the custodian can let a second listener test the box.

slips.title: The two blades
slips.opening: Harl is weighing a pair of warped shears against his pay chit. One blade was bought by the Warden’s office. The other was ground in a kitchen by somebody left off the payroll.
slips.first: Close the blades on a doubled strip of waste paper
slips.discovery: A stepped cut crosses both layers. The coarse teeth are an exact fit for a proviso torn from a river sheet.

routes.action: Leave the sample on the workers’ gate
routes.consequence: The grinder can claim a wage in public. Harl will have to say who gave him the shears.

routes.action: Put the shears and the pay chit in the worker’s hands
routes.consequence: The grinder can speak when ready. The public ledger keeps its blank for another shift.

slips.title: Three notches in the first press
slips.opening: Liesl keeps the press oiled with the money from her father’s first order. The customer’s name has faded. Three pinholes cross the word deposit.
slips.first: Pull a blind impression without ink
slips.discovery: Three little ridges come up. A stray ivory-coloured thread is still caught under the last ridge.

routes.action: Clip the impression beside the daybook
routes.consequence: Strangers can compare it. Liesl can hear people guessing her father’s name from the doorway.

routes.action: Give Liesl the first pull for her father
routes.consequence: He can recognise his old press by touch. Somebody must bring the second copy to the woods.

slips.title: The unfinished promise
slips.opening: Penrose keeps two pilots’ orders folded together. One says to issue a warning immediately. The other has a blank after the words “come back when”.
slips.first: Thread the two slips on the same wet peg
slips.discovery: The lines meet at the peg. Two different people had agreed to return for a second sounding.

routes.action: Fly the two slips together as a signal
routes.consequence: The crews see the promise. Penrose stays on deck as living ballast until the tide turns.

routes.action: Ask the two pilots to carry one slip apiece
routes.consequence: Both can call for the return trip. A new crew has to find the pilots before it can hear the whole agreement.

slips.title: One chair in the wrong wings
slips.opening: Lucan is trying to return a chair after the show. A gold ticket under the seat is for a market hearing, and the person who used it cannot stand for long.
slips.first: Turn the chair by its back and read the footmarks
slips.discovery: The chair moved between two meetings while both rolls still listed the witness as seated.

routes.action: Put the empty chair in the interval light
routes.consequence: The audience sees where somebody was counted twice. The understudy gives up her warm seat.

routes.action: Take the ticket to the witness’s own seat
routes.consequence: The witness can mark the error in private. The audience repeats the larger crowd count for another night.

slips.title: The audience of one extra coat
slips.opening: Cass folds a paid cloak over an empty stool. “If a clerk counted it, the clerk got paid. That was our arrangement.” A drawing of a sore foot sticks out of the pocket.
slips.first: Set the cloak and the stool on separate marks
slips.discovery: Two admission tags use the same worn corner. One purchased a reserved seat while its owner was elsewhere.

routes.action: Set the spare tag on the public scales
routes.consequence: The crowd can see why two tickets made one witness. Cass has to refund a day’s commission.

routes.action: Send the spare tag home inside the cloak
routes.consequence: The owner gets their money first. The empty stool looks occupied until close.

slips.title: Two villages in one minute
slips.opening: On the weir wheel Dorran has scratched a notch for every warning he heard. One notch has been cut so deep it looks like two.
slips.first: Turn the warning drum while the lower wheel rests
slips.discovery: The upper wheel sounds before the lower village is within earshot. Dorran had counted the echo as a reply.

routes.action: Mark the silent interval on both gateposts
routes.consequence: Both crews can see how long the answer takes. Dorran will have to stand through the interval again.

routes.action: Lend the moving drum to the listening family
routes.consequence: They can hear exactly what Dorran heard. At the gate his crew must count without it.

slips.title: A house the model cannot reach
slips.opening: Nyle points at the blank between two homes on the route. The cart served the painted model beautifully. A real woman had to cross the canal to fetch her books.
slips.first: Roll the little cart until its axle catches
slips.discovery: A pencilled doorway sits one wheel-width outside the model. The larger cart never actually crossed.

routes.action: Paint the doorway at its measured distance
routes.consequence: The scale looks less tidy. The new driver can find the right house.

routes.action: Ask the woman to guide a full-size trial
routes.consequence: She can show the driver a safer turn. We owe her a morning at her own work.

slips.title: The breath after the warning
slips.opening: Tolly's hand is on the mute button when a child in the recording starts to answer the old warning. “Her family asked me to look after that breath.”
slips.first: Run the two receivers until the unwound thread tightens
slips.discovery: The child began speaking during the interval the upper crew recorded as silence.

routes.action: Play only the space before the family’s answer
routes.consequence: The upper crew hears its own wait. Tolly sits ready to stop anyone who winds further.

routes.action: Give the family the rewind handle
routes.consequence: They choose who hears the answer. The other crew must return when the family can receive them.

slips.title: The knuckle in the paper canal
slips.opening: Sabine's exhibition bridge fits the painted canal exactly. A builder stops a paper cart with one knuckle. “That’s where my mother's door would be.”
slips.first: Turn the street tray until the doorstep meets the bridge
slips.discovery: The model was trimmed to fit its case. The last straight cut removed a house and made the route look complete.

routes.action: Leave the house outside the glass
routes.consequence: A visitor can test what the frame left out. Sabine loses the prize for the cleanest model.

routes.action: Lend the open tray to the canal builder
routes.consequence: The mother gets to tell the story first. At the fair an empty socket marks the missing exhibit.

pairs: The lamp had never run on coins. A carrier used the coin to hold her instructions upright. Wystan folds a new slip and Mabry lets her boy put the farthing back in his purse.

Laid together, the two cuts show a household copy shortened for packing and a second cut made at the office. Osric takes the family name out of the accusation. Harl leaves the office signature for the Water Commons witnesses.
The second sounding was a promise Vesper helped write. She had pressed the paper flat with her knee while Elsbet drew the tide. The quarrel came over whether the first warning could travel alone.
The three notes fit the ridges of the press. The deposit came through a river office before the Gilded Seal sold its first copy. Liesl had blamed her father for a price he had never set.
The market ticket fits the empty theatre chair. A person needed an accessible seat in two places on one afternoon. It was the attendance books that claimed they sat in both at once.
The two records share the same wheel click. What sounded like silence upriver was the time a child needed to answer downstream. Dorran sits beside Tolly for one whole turn of the reel.
Where did the last house go?

The gutter of the district map fits the trimmed edge of the model. A woman kept her house and lost her delivery route because a piece of paper had to fit a frame. Sabine carries her next parcel by hand.
